question: Can GTK2 hide the full-cell dotted focus outline on selected IconView items without removing keyboard focus indication when no item is selected?
runtime: GTK 2.24.33 native GtkIconView in private Xvfb; selection mode MULTIPLE; cursor item focused; selected_count=0; no live application changed.

normal_focus_width.result: A dotted focus outline remains visible around the cursor item while no item is selected.

focus_width_zero.style: GtkWidget::focus-line-width = 0 on the GtkIconView style only
focus_width_zero.result: The focus outline disappears with selected_count=0 even though the widget still has focus. With an item selected, the KDE selection fill remains, but that does not cover the no-selection keyboard-navigation state.

decision: Do not set the IconView focus line width to zero globally. It would erase the only visible keyboard focus cue when multiple-selection mode has a cursor item but no selected item. Preserve the existing focus line until a supported, more precise focus treatment has evidence.
limits: No matching VUE unselected-but-focused XmpIcon state was obtained; this is a GTK2 safety probe, not a historical match claim.
No product GTK2 RC, palette, user setting, XChat process, VM or MAME capture hook was changed by this probe.
next: Continue I167/GTK2 with a measurable control or state. Preserve keyboard focus visibility and keep the R200 full-cell selection geometry gap explicit.
